s: The Vice-President of India is elected by means of which electoral system?
o: Simple majority voting by secret ballot
Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and open ballot
Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot
x: Article 66 provides for proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, and the election is conducted by secret ballot.
tq: Discriminate between the voting method, ballot method and majority system rather than recalling only one feature.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a qualification for election as Vice-President of India?
o: Qualification for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
Qualification for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha
x: The Vice-President must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old and qualified for election to the Rajya Sabha. Qualification for election to the Lok Sabha is not the prescribed condition.
tq: Find the one swapped constitutional qualification among closely related House requirements.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the normal term of office of the Vice-President of India?
o: Four years from the date of election, without continuation thereafter
Six years from entering office, with continuation only after parliamentary approval
Five years from the date of nomination, with no possibility of re-election
Five years from entering office, with continuation until the successor enters office
x: The Vice-President holds office for five years from the date of entering office and continues beyond that period until the successor enters office. The Vice-President is eligible for re-election any number of times.
tq: Separate the fixed term, commencement point and holdover provision instead of treating them as one date rule.

s: The oath or affirmation of office to the Vice-President of India is administered by the
x: Article 69 provides that the oath or affirmation of office to the Vice-President is administered by the President or a person appointed by the President for that purpose.
tq: Apply the ‘who administers the oath?’ distinction among constitutional authorities.

s:
Consider the following statements about the removal of the Vice-President of India:
1. The resolution must originate in the Rajya Sabha.
2. The resolution requires an effective majority of the Rajya Sabha.
3. The Lok Sabha must agree to the resolution by a simple majority.
4. The Constitution specifies grounds on which the Vice-President may be removed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Removal is initiated in the Rajya Sabha, requires a majority of all the then members of that House, and must be agreed to by the Lok Sabha by simple majority. The Constitution does not state grounds for this removal.
tq: Break the removal procedure into origin, majority, second-House approval and grounds.

s: A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President of India can be moved only after giving a minimum notice of
x: A minimum notice of 14 days is required before moving the resolution for removal of the Vice-President in the Rajya Sabha.
tq: Use the exact notice period as the decisive numerical discriminator.

s: If the Vice-President of India is acting as President, who presides over the sittings of the Rajya Sabha?
o: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: While acting as President, the Vice-President ceases to perform the functions of Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Deputy Chairman presides over the Rajya Sabha during that period.
tq: Follow the consequence of temporary assumption of the President’s office on the Vice-President’s ex-officio role.
sec: Vice-President - election, term, removal, ex-officio role, disputes  [APPSC]

s: While acting as President of India, the Vice-President is entitled to draw the salary of the
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: When acting as President, the Vice-President ceases to function as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and draws the President’s salary rather than the Chairman’s salary.
tq: Apply the office actually being performed, not the office ordinarily held.
sec: Vice-President - election, term, removal, ex-officio role, disputes  [APPSC]

s: As Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Vice-President ordinarily exercises
o: A casting vote in the event of an equality of votes
A vote only on Money Bills
x: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote when the votes are equally divided.
tq: Distinguish an ordinary vote from a casting vote in a presiding-officer question.

s: A vacancy in the office of the Vice-President of India is to be filled
o: Within six months of the vacancy in every case
As soon as possible, without a constitutionally prescribed six-month deadline
Within one year, after approval by the Supreme Court
Only at the next general election to the Lok Sabha
x: Article 68 requires an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President as soon as possible. Unlike the vacancy in the office of President, no six-month deadline is prescribed for this election.
tq: Compare the vacancy rules for President and Vice-President, especially the presence or absence of a fixed deadline.
sec: Vice-President - election, term, removal, ex-officio role, disputes  [APPSC]

s: When the office of the President falls vacant, the Vice-President acts as President until
o: The Council of Ministers elects a successor
The next session of Parliament begins
A new President is elected, which must take place within six months of the vacancy
The remaining term of the previous President expires
x: The Vice-President acts as President until a new President is elected. The election to fill the presidential vacancy must be held within six months of the vacancy.
tq: Identify the event that ends the acting arrangement and distinguish it from the former President’s remaining term.
sec: Vice-President - election, term, removal, ex-officio role, disputes  [APPSC]

s: Which constitutional provision deals with disputes relating to the election of the Vice-President of India?
x: Article 71 places disputes relating to the election of the President or Vice-President under the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding judicial authority over Presidential and Vice-Presidential election disputes:
1. The 39th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975 removed the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction over such election disputes.
2. The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 restored that jurisdiction.
3. The Election Commission of India conducts these elections under the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 39th Amendment removed the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction over the specified election disputes, while the 44th Amendment restored it. The elections are conducted by the Election Commission under the 1952 Act.
tq: Arrange the amendment reversal and the conducting authority as separate legal facts.

12 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
10 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
20 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha

s: A member of Parliament disqualified for defection under the Tenth Schedule is, by virtue of Article 75(1B),
o: eligible only after approval by the Election Commission
permanently barred from becoming a Union Minister
ineligible to be appointed Union Minister until re-elected to Parliament
eligible to be appointed Union Minister immediately after disqualification

s: With reference to the size of a State Council of Ministers, which one of the following is correct?
o: It shall not exceed 10 per cent of the Assembly strength and has no minimum floor.
It shall be fixed uniformly at 15 ministers for every State.
It shall not exceed 20 per cent of the Assembly strength, subject to a minimum of 10 ministers.
It shall not exceed 15 per cent of the Assembly strength, subject to a minimum of 12 ministers.
x: Article 164(1A), inserted by the 91st Amendment, limits a State Council of Ministers to 15 per cent of the Assembly strength, while prescribing a minimum of 12 ministers.
tq: Check both limbs of the rule: the percentage ceiling and the statutory minimum floor.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a constitutionally prescribed rank of a Union Minister?

s:

3. Deputy Ministers form one of the conventionally recognised ministerial ranks.

Article 67 — Oath or affirmation of the Vice-President
Article 71 — Election procedure by single transferable vote

o: A non-member cannot be repeatedly reappointed as Minister without getting elected.
Only a member of the Lok Sabha can be appointed as a Minister.
A non-member may be reappointed as Minister indefinitely without election.

The President may remove any Minister independently of the Prime Minister.

o: The Prime Minister can be removed only by the Supreme Court.
The Prime Minister holds office for life unless removed by impeachment.
The Prime Minister continues in office while commanding the confidence of the Lok Sabha, subject to the President's pleasure in the constitutional sense.

The Prime Minister is the de jure head of State and the President is only a ceremonial officer of Parliament.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the position of the Prime Minister in the United Kingdom from that in India?
o: The UK Prime Minister must belong to the House of Lords, whereas the Indian Prime Minister must belong to the Lok Sabha.
The UK Prime Minister must belong to the House of Commons, whereas the Indian Prime Minister may belong to either House of Parliament.
Both the UK and Indian Prime Ministers must be members of the lower House.
Neither the UK nor the Indian Prime Minister may be a member of the upper House.
x: The UK Prime Minister must belong to the House of Commons, while the Indian Prime Minister may be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
tq: Use the House-membership distinction to separate the British and Indian parliamentary arrangements.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the tenure of the Prime Minister of India?

The Constitution fixes a maximum of two terms for the Prime Minister.
The Prime Minister must retire after completing one Lok Sabha term.
